summary: The article surveys a new wave of performance artists who combine technology with live performance, using AR, VR, AI, projection mapping, live coding, sensor-driven sound and social media. It profiles specific artists and works across US cities from September 2023 to March 2024. The common thread is blurring the line between performer and audience and making technology a core part of the art.
one_line: A tour of US performance artists using AR, VR, AI, projection mapping, live coding and social media to redefine live art and audience engagement.
key_facts: Jameson DuPree's performance series 'Sensory Overload' has run in New York City since September 7, 2023, using AR headsets so spectators can take part.
DuPree's piece 'Fractured Horizons' lets viewers construct and deconstruct the space around them while he performs an emotionally charged dance narrative.
The Los Angeles collective 'Code Motion', founded by Alex Rivera, staged its first show on October 15, 2023, using AI to generate choreography.
Code Motion dancers wear motion capture suits while AI algorithms analyze their movements and suggest new, often unpredictable sequences.
Clara Kim's installation 'Resonant Tides' was featured at the San Francisco Sound Art Festival on November 21, 2023, with sensors triggering soundscapes via interconnected synthesizers and samplers.
Kim uses binaural beats and spatial sound technologies to create deep physiological engagement.
Luca Garcia performed 'Ephemeral Canvas' on December 3, 2023, in the roundabout theatre of Atlanta, combining live painting with 3D projection mapping.
Evelyn Torres launched the VR experience 'Boundless Realms' in Seattle on January 8, 2024, where participants wearing VR headsets influence different storylines.
Hiro Tanaka's 'CodeStream', first performed February 20, 2024, in Denver, uses live coding to produce generative art in real time, exposing his creative process.
Miami-based artist Sophia Cortez's 'The Collective Pulse', live-streamed March 14, 2024, integrated live audience reactions into the visuals, creating a feedback loop.
Artists increasingly live-stream shows and use audience input from platforms like Twitter and Instagram live to steer performances in real time.
Algorithmic choreography has sparked debates about creativity and spontaneity in dance.
